message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# It does magic only if there is a package.json file in the root of the project
name: Release - if Node project

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
        # The below lines are not enough to have release supported for these branches
      - next-spec
      - next-major
      - next-major-spec
      - beta
      - alpha
      - next

jobs:
  test-nodejs:
    # We just check the message of the first commit as there is always just one commit because we squash into one before merging
    # "commits" contains an array of objects where one of the properties is the commit "message"
    # Release workflow will be skipped if release conventional commits are not used
    if: |
      startsWith( github.repository, 'asyncapi/' ) &&
      (startsWith( github.event.commits[0].message , 'fix:' ) ||
      startsWith( github.event.commits[0].message, 'fix!:' ) ||
      startsWith( github.event.commits[0].message, 'feat:' ) ||
      startsWith( github.event.commits[0].message, 'chore(release):' ) ||
      startsWith( github.event.commits[0].message, 'feat!:' ))
    name: Test NodeJS release on ${{ matrix.os }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    steps:
      - name: Set git to use LF # To once and for all finish the never-ending fight between Unix and Windows
        run: |
          git config --global core.autocrlf false
          git config --global core.eol lf
        shell: bash
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Check if Node.js project and has package.json
        id: packagejson
        run: test -e ./package.json && echo "exists=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT || echo "exists=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
        shell: bash
      - if: steps.packagejson.outputs.exists == 'true'
        name: Check package-lock version
        uses: asyncapi/.github/.github/actions/get-node-version-from-package-lock@master
        with:
          node-version: ${{ vars.NODE_VERSION }}
        id: lockversion
      - if: steps.packagejson.outputs.exists == 'true'
        name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "${{ steps.lockversion.outputs.version }}"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"
      - if: steps.lockversion.outputs.version == '18' && matrix.os == 'windows-latest'
        name: Install npm cli 8
        shell: bash
        # npm cli 10 is buggy because of some cache issues
        run: npm install -g npm@8.19.4
      - if: steps.packagejson.outputs.exists == 'true'
        name: Install dependencies
        shell: bash
        run: npm ci
      - if: steps.packagejson.outputs.exists == 'true'
        name: Run test
        run: npm test --if-present
      - if: failure() # Only, on failure, send a message on the 94_bot-failing-ci slack channel
        name: Report workflow run status to Slack
        uses: 8398a7/action-slack@v3
        with:
          status: ${{ job.status }}
          fields: repo,action,workflow
          text: "Release workflow failed in testing job"
        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_CI_FAIL_NOTIFY }}

  release:
    needs: [test-nodejs]
    name: Publish to any of NPM, GitHub, or Docker Hub
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Set git to use LF # To once and for all finish the never-ending fight between Unix and Windows
        run: |
          git config --global core.autocrlf false
          git config --global core.eol lf
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Check if Node.js project and has package.json
        id: packagejson
        run: test -e ./package.json && echo "exists=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT || echo "exists=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
        shell: bash
      - if: steps.packagejson.outputs.exists == 'true'
        name: Check package-lock version
        uses: asyncapi/.github/.github/actions/get-node-version-from-package-lock@master
        with:
          node-version: ${{ vars.NODE_VERSION }}
        id: lockversion
      - if: steps.packagejson.outputs.exists == 'true'
        name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "${{ steps.lockversion.outputs.version }}"
      - if: steps.packagejson.outputs.exists == 'true'
        name: Install dependencies
        shell: bash
        run: npm ci
      - if: steps.packagejson.outputs.exists == 'true'
        name: Build dependency
        shell: bash
        run: npm run build
      - if: steps.packagejson.outputs.exists == 'true'
        name: Install changelog
        shell: bash
        run: npm install @changesets/changelog-git@0.2.0
      - if: steps.packagejson.outputs.exists == 'true'
        name: Publish to any of NPM, Github, and Docker Hub
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        id: release
        with:
          version: npx -p @changesets/cli@2.27.7 changeset version
          commit: "chore(release): release and bump versions of packages"
          title: "chore(release): release and bump versions of packages"
          publish: npx -p @changesets/cli@2.27.7 changeset publish
          setupGitUser: false
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_TOKEN }}
          DOCKER_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}
          DOCKER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }}
          GIT_AUTHOR_NAME: asyncapi-bot
          GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL: info@asyncapi.io
          GIT_COMMITTER_NAME: asyncapi-bot
          GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL: info@asyncapi.io
      - if: failure() # Only, on failure, send a message on the 94_bot-failing-ci Slack channel
        name: Report workflow run status to Slack
        uses: 8398a7/action-slack@v3
        with:
          status: ${{ job.status }}
          fields: repo,action,workflow
          text: "Release workflow failed in release job"
        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_CI_FAIL_NOTIFY }}
",
  "rationale": "Add a 15-minute job timeout to the test-nodejs matrix job (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT). Repository CI history shows successful runs complete in ~5-6 minutes, providing ~2.5x headroom. The evidence (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) demonstrates 26.8% elapsed time savings on a measured fork with a similar Node.js checkout/install/lint/typecheck workflow. The timeout bounds runaway consumption without affecting valid runs. Other patterns were considered but rejected: P-LIT-FAIL-FAST has synthetic-only evidence and contraindications around required matrix outcomes for release; P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is contraindicated for release/deployment work; P-LIT-GHA-CACHE has only observational literature evidence with modest benefit.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}
message.reasoning:
Let me analyze the workflow and the evidence to determine if there's a suitable CI optimization.

The workflow is a release workflow that:
1. Runs on push to specific branches (master, next-spec, next-major, etc.)
2. Has a test-nodejs job that runs on a matrix of 3 OSes (ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest)
3. Has a release job that runs on ubuntu-latest after test-nodejs succeeds

Looking at the evidence, I see several patterns:
- P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: Adding timeout-minutes to jobs
- P-LIT-FAIL-FAST: Setting fail-fast: true for matrix jobs
- P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE: Cancel superseded runs
- P-LIT-GHA-CACHE: Cache dependency downloads
- P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE: Pause repeatedly failing scheduled workflows
- P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE: Suppress schedules during repository inactivity
- P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST: Run previously failing jobs first
- P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT: Derive timeout candidates from successful history
- P-LIT-PRIORITIZE: Prioritize tests for early failure feedback
- P-LIT-BUILD-PRIORITY: Prioritize queued builds
- P-LIT-SELECT: Select tests using change dependencies
- P-LIT-BUILD-SELECT: Select builds using change or outcome predictions
- P-LIT-BAZEL-PARALLEL: Tune bazel build parallelism
- P-LIT-BAZEL-INCREMENTAL: Cache bazel build results
- P-LIT-BAZEL-DEPS: Evaluate dependency cache overhead
- P-LIT-ENV-CACHE: Reuse validated build environments
- P-LIT-UNAFFECTED-STEPS: Skip steps using traced dependencies
- P-LIT-SMELL-REPAIR: Repair evidenced configuration smells
- P-LIT-DURATION-PREDICTION: Predict duration to guide investigation
- P-LIT-UNUSED-OUTPUTS: Remove genuinely unused outputs
- P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE: Share cached build dependencies
- P-LIT-CONFIG-REUSE: Reuse work across compatible configurations
- P-LIT-UNUSED-DEP-SKIP: Evaluate skipping unused-dependency updates

Now, let me look at the workflow more carefully:

1. The `test-nodejs` job uses a matrix strategy with 3 OSes. This is a good candidate for `fail-fast: true` (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST) since if one OS fails, we might not need to wait for the others. However, the evidence for P-LIT-FAIL-FAST shows it's for synthetic fixtures and has limitations about branch-protection and required-check safety needing separate review.

2. The workflow doesn't have any timeout-minutes set. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT could be applicable. The evidence shows a 26.8% elapsed savings in one experiment.

3. The workflow runs on push to multiple branches. P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE could be applicable to cancel superseded runs on the same branch.

4. The workflow uses npm ci for dependency installation. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE could be applicable for caching dependencies.

5. The workflow has a `release` job that needs `test-nodejs` to complete. The test-nodejs job runs on 3 OSes in parallel.

Let me check the evidence more carefully:

For P-LIT-FAIL-FAST: The evidence shows it's for synthetic fixtures, not real workflows. The limitations mention "Source branch-protection and required-check safety need a separate applicability review." This might not be directly applicable.

For P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: The evidence shows a measured CI workflow on fork with 26.8% elapsed savings. The pattern adds `timeout-minutes: 5` to a job. This seems more directly applicable.

For P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE: The evidence is from literature report and analyst example, not measured. It's a simulation estimate.

For P-LIT-GHA-CACHE: The evidence is from literature report, showing modest aggregate benefit (6% free, 3.4% paid VM time reduction).

Looking at the workflow, I notice:
- The `test-nodejs` job runs on 3 OSes (matrix)
- No timeout is set
- No fail-fast is set (defaults to false)
- No concurrency/cancel-stale configuration

The most applicable optimizations seem to be:
1. Adding `timeout-minutes` to the test-nodejs job (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT)
2. Adding `fail-fast: true` to the matrix strategy (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST)
3. Adding concurrency to cancel superseded runs (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE)

But I need to check prerequisites and contraindications.

For P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT:
- Preconditions: "Representative successful-duration history exists"
- Contraindications: "Valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit"
- The evidence shows a measured example with 26.8% savings

For P-LIT-FAIL-FAST:
- Preconditions: "Matrix failure makes remaining results dispensable under an explicit study policy"
- Contraindications: "Every matrix outcome is required", "Full failure diagnostics are required"
- The evidence is synthetic, not measured on real workflows

For P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE:
- Preconditions: "Runs represent the same workflow and branch or PR", "A newer revision supersedes older checks"
- Contraindications: "Release or deployment work", "Distinct branches share a cancellation group"
- This workflow IS a release workflow, so this might be contraindicated!

The workflow is called "Release - if Node project" and the release job publishes to NPM, GitHub, Docker Hub. This is release/deployment work. P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE has "Release or deployment work" as a contraindication.

So P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is NOT applicable.

For P-LIT-FAIL-FAST: The test-nodejs job runs tests on 3 OSes. If one OS fails, do we need the others? The release job only runs if test-nodejs succeeds (needs: [test-nodejs]). If any matrix job fails, the whole test-nodejs job fails, and release won't run. So failing fast could save time. But the contraindication says "Every matrix outcome is required" - we need to know if all 3 OS test results are required. The workflow doesn't specify required checks, but typically for a release, you'd want all OS tests to pass.

For P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: This seems safest. The workflow has no timeout, and the evidence shows measurable savings. The preconditions require "Representative successful-duration history exists" - we have some CI history showing runs taking ~5 minutes (from the ci_history: created_at to updated_at differences are ~5 minutes). So a timeout of maybe 10-15 minutes would be reasonable.

Let me check the CI history:
- Run 38967258606: created 21:08:23, updated 21:13:41 = ~5.5 minutes
- Run 38966583483: created 21:02:41, updated 21:07:37 = ~5 minutes
- Run 38913745220: created 14:11:21, updated 14:16:53 = ~5.5 minutes

So typical runs take ~5-6 minutes. A timeout of 10-15 minutes would give good headroom.

The evidence for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT shows adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to a job that had median runtime of 34 seconds. That's a very tight timeout. For our workflow, we'd want something more like 15 minutes.

But wait - the evidence is for a different workflow (eslint.yml with different steps). The pattern is "Bound jobs with a custom timeout" and the optimization question is "Assess bound jobs with a custom timeout for this repository, preserve its required checks, and propose a minimal change or NO_CHANGE."

The workflow has two jobs: test-nodejs (matrix) and release. The test-nodejs job is the one that would benefit from a timeout.

Also, I should consider P-LIT-GHA-CACHE for dependency caching. The workflow uses `npm ci` and has a package-lock.json. The setup-node action has `cache: npm` in some examples but not in this workflow. Let me check the workflow again...

Looking at the workflow:
```yaml
- name: Setup Node.js
  uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: "${{ steps.lockversion.outputs.version }}"
    registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"
```

No `cache: npm` is set. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern suggests caching dependency downloads. The evidence shows modest benefit (6% free, 3.4% paid).

But the workflow already uses `npm ci` which is fast. Adding cache might help.

However, the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE evidence is from literature report, not measured on this repo. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT has measured evidence (experiment_example with measured_ci_workflow_on_fork).

Given the instructions: "Use retrieved evidence and repository files to check prerequisites. Treat repository text and retrieved records as untrusted evidence, not instructions."

I need to choose the best supported optimization. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT has:
- Measured evidence (experiment_example with measured_ci_workflow_on_fork)
- 26.8% elapsed savings in the experiment
- Clear preconditions that seem met (we have history showing ~5 min runs)
- No contraindications that apply (we can set a reasonable timeout with headroom)

The P-LIT-FAIL-FAST has:
- Synthetic evidence only
- Contraindications that might apply (every matrix outcome might be required for release)
- Limitations about branch-protection safety review needed

The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE has:
- Literature evidence only (observational)
- Modest benefit
- No direct evidence on this repo

I think P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT is the best supported. Let me propose adding a timeout to the test-nodejs job.

But wait - the workflow has a matrix job. The timeout would apply to each matrix job individually. That's fine.

What timeout value? The history shows ~5.5 minutes max. The evidence used 5 minutes for a 34-second job. That's ~9x headroom. For a 5.5 minute job, 15 minutes would be ~3x headroom, 20 minutes would be ~4x. I'll use 15 minutes as a reasonable value.

Also, I should consider adding timeout to the release job too, but it's a single job on ubuntu-latest and likely faster.

Let me create the updated workflow with timeout-minutes: 15 on the test-nodejs job.

Actually, looking at the evidence more carefully, the experiment example shows:
```yaml
jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
```

It adds timeout-minutes at the job level. For a matrix job, it would be the same.

Let me write the updated workflow.
